messages.author: 340ab77615aafcd1
messages.subject: Sliding window analysis function
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to use the additional function called 'slide' from the extension to ctmm at https://github.com/ctmm-initiative/window. I can't quite figure out how to get that package to install; remotes::install_github doesn't recognize it. If I follow the instructions on the page, I do get the repository on my system, but it doesn't actually seem to allow for use of the new function. Trying the function base::source to read the individual files doesn't throw up any errors, but it doesn't mean that my computer can recognize 'slide' either. What is the intended way to get access to that function? Is it not actually ready for public use?

Thanks,
Joshua Johnson

messages.author: 26f783f241741dbf
messages.subject: Re: Sliding window analysis function
parts:
Hi Joshua,

These functions are not directly compiled with the ctmm package, so loading each of the scripts in the repository as you mentioned would be the correct way to use them. Going through the R scripts using the source() function should load in all the necessary functions into your current environment, but if that fails, you can always just manually run through all the lines in each of the scripts.

That being said, I will refine some of the guides, as well as add in some extra functionalities that have not yet been published within the next week or two, which may help. I will notify everyone here once that has been reflected in the GitHub repository.

Best,
Nozomu Hirama

messages.author: 26f783f241741dbf
messages.subject: Re: Sliding window analysis function
parts:
Hi all, 

I have updated the GitHub repository to include a new argument in the slide function called "release". By setting release = TRUE, users can now examine trends in terms of days elapsed since release/tracking using the slide() function. This can also work with populations where different individuals were released or began tagging at different times. The example_usage script now includes this "release = TRUE" case. I have also modified the function to take in entire population datasets even if there are gaps or periods with only one individual with available tracking data. For each window, the function will only use the individuals with data available during that window.

Please feel free to ask any questions or point out any issues regarding these sliding window function.

Best,
Nozomu

Hi
Looking at it again, it still doesn't work as I'd expect it to. Looking into the code I think I can see a couple places where it keeps breaking
1) in main.R (which defines the function slide), after making the summary of the window estimate, it just changes the row names without checking if all the rows exist, and throws up errors if they don't
2) It doesn't check if the confidence intervals for the summary of the window estimate actually exists and often throws up errors

[1] "area"

and the function has no way to deal with it.

I can get these working but I figure other might have the same problem

Thanks,
Joshua

messages.subject: Re: Sliding window analysis function

Thanks for letting me know. I've fixed this and updated the GitHub repository. Could you try again after redownloading the new scripts? I believe it should now work for estimating area (both for individuals and populations), but I still need to make some fixes for the other parameter estimates. This unusual summary output is likely due to the window not having a large enough effective sample size to estimate a valid home range estimates, so I have fixed the code to return these as NA. Let me know if you are still encountering issues.

Best,
Nozomu
